final_candidates.decision_summary: Position 158 lies in the Sa antigenic site and Asn is the canonical escape residue at this position in H1 HA, naturally tolerated in circulating strains. High escape potential with low expected folding cost.
Residue 163 is a well-documented Sa-site escape position in human H1; the charge switch on the exposed loop favors antibody escape with minimal structural perturbation.
Charge reversal at the Sa-site surface loop adjacent to 158 should disrupt antibody binding while the surface-exposed location suggests modest fitness cost and preserved folding.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 Sa-site candidates are stably ranked and further self-iteration without new evidence is unlikely to improve the selection.

history.rationale: Residue in the Sb antigenic site of the HA globular head; introducing an N-linked glycosylation motif can sterically shield nearby epitopes while being a conservative surface change.
S158 lies in the Sa antigenic site; Asn at 158 is the canonical glycosylation-linked escape residue in H1 HA and is naturally tolerated.
Charge reversal at a solvent-exposed Sb-site residue commonly disrupts antibody binding with minimal impact on folding.
Adjacent Sa-site charge reversal; surface loop position suggests modest fitness cost and good escape potential.
Sb-site surface residue; side-chain identity change alters epitope electrostatics and is distal from the receptor-binding pocket.
163 is a well-known Sa-site escape position (163T/K selection in human H1); charge switch at surface-exposed loop favors escape with low folding cost.
Exposed Ca-region residue in the globular head; charge swap is a classic escape mechanism and surface lysines tolerate substitution well.
169 falls in the Ca antigenic site; Lys-to-Glu reversal on exposed loop plausibly disrupts antibody binding.
Adjacent Ca-site residue to 169; an alternative charge-reversal escape option in the same immunodominant patch.
Ca-site surface charge reversal, similar rationale to K169E but possibly redundant with it.
Lysine in the Cb/Sa-adjacent head region; exposed basic residue substitutions frequently reduce antibody recognition with low fitness cost.
Ca-site residue near receptor-binding region; charge reversal could aid escape but slightly higher fitness risk.
Surface residue in the Ca antigenic region; polar-to-amide change can remove a key antibody contact while preserving local structure.
Conservative substitution in Ca-site loop, likely tolerated but escape effect may be modest.
Sa-region residue near the receptor-binding site rim; may alter antigenicity, but proximity to the sialic-acid pocket carries some fitness risk.
Sb-site glycine insertion of charged residue risks local conformational perturbation near RBS; keep but do not promote.
Charge reversal at an exposed head residue in the Sa/Cb antigenic vicinity; expected to perturb antibody epitopes.
Sb-site charge reversal; 187-190 region is a known escape hotspot, providing site diversity versus Sa/Ca candidates.
Exposed head-domain serine; potential glycan addition could mask epitopes, though location is less clearly antigenic so confidence is lower.
Position 102 is not in a major H1 antigenic site, so escape benefit is likely minimal; drop to keep pool focused.

rejection.reason: Position 102 is not in a major H1 antigenic site, so escape benefit is likely minimal; drop to keep pool focused.
